title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from this and the neighbouring pages. K is a number field and Γ = Gal(K̄/K). X is a curve over K with a Belyi-type map. C is (most likely) the open part of X lying over U_{0,3} = P^1 − {0,1,∞}, and g : C → U_{0,3} is finite étale, defined over K. I_0 is a set of K-rational base points (possibly tangential) of U_{0,3}. I is a set of K-rational points of C lying over I_0. The saturation is I' = g^{-1}(I_0), the full fibre. The aim is to show that the action of Γ on the profinite fundamental groupoid of U_{0,3} with base points I_0 determines its action on the fundamental groupoid of X. This is the Belyi-type reduction of all curves to U_{0,3}. It also prepares a list of necessary conditions for an automorphism of Π̂_1(U_{0,3}; I_0) to come from Galois.

Step 1. The functor g_* : Π̂_1(C; I') → Π̂_1(U_{0,3}; I_0) is faithful. That is, for x, y in I' the map Hom_{Π̂_1(C)}(x,y) → Hom_{Π̂_1(U_{0,3})}(g x, g y) is injective. Reason: a finite étale cover identifies π̂_1(C,x) with an open subgroup of π̂_1(U_{0,3}, g x), and path classes lift uniquely once the starting point is fixed. The functor is Γ-equivariant, so the Γ-action on Π̂_1(C, I') is the restriction of the action downstairs. The marginal note 'via (39)+(40)' points to earlier formulas, presumably this covering description.

Step 2. Π̂_1(X, I) is a Γ-equivariant quotient of Π̂_1(C, I): fill in the punctures, i.e. kill inertia. So it too is determined.

Step 3 (methodological remark). One did not strictly need to pass from I to I', since I' need not lie in C(K). The conclusion 'action on Π̂_1(U_{0,3}, I_0) ⇒ action on Π̂_1(X, I)' holds with I alone. Still, comparing the two groupoids as groupoids with operator group Γ is much easier with the saturated vertex set I'. If the vertices of I' 'se baladent' (are permuted) under Γ, replace Γ by an open subgroup Γ' fixing them, i.e. enlarge K.

Next page. This yields necessary conditions for a vertex-fixing automorphism Θ of Π̂_1(U_{0,3}; I_0) to come from some u ∈ Γ. For every étale cover C over K, Θ must lift to an automorphism Θ_C of Π̂_1(C; f^{-1}(I_0) ∩ C(K)) that is the identity on vertices. Allowing a power Θ^n handles vertices that are not rational.
errors: No mathematical error. Faithfulness of the induced functor for a finite étale cover is correct, and so is its compatibility with profinite completion (open subgroups).
Conditional on fibre points not being K-rational, the Γ-action permutes vertices of I'. The text itself repairs this by passing to an open subgroup Γ'.

ideas.what: Finite étale cover induces a faithful (injective on Hom-sets) Γ-equivariant functor of profinite fundamental groupoids with many base points
ideas.modern_name: Fundamental groupoid of a covering; étale fundamental groupoid with several base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA1); groupoid viewpoint widely used (Deligne 1989 for many base points/tangential)
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (fundamental groupoid); Esquisse d'un programme (groupoids with several base points)

ideas.what: Galois action on π̂_1 of any curve over a number field is determined by the action on π̂_1(P^1−{0,1,∞}) with rational base points, via a Belyi map
ideas.modern_name: Belyi reduction / faithfulness of G_Q on π̂_1(U_{0,3})

ideas.what: Saturating the base-point set to the full fibre, passing to an open subgroup of Γ so that vertices are fixed
ideas.modern_name: Base-change to a finite extension; Γ-groupoids with fixed vertices

ideas.what: (Next page) Necessary condition for Θ ∈ Aut(Π̂_1(U_{0,3}; I_0)) to come from Galois: liftability to the groupoids of all covers defined over K, fixing the rational vertices
ideas.modern_name: Characterization of the image of G_Q in Out(π̂_1(U_{0,3})); cf. GT (Drinfeld, Ihara) and Pop's I/OM
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses the Teichmüller-tower description of G_Q, but not this specific cover-by-cover condition

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates the candidate description of the Galois image cover by cover. An automorphism of the fundamental groupoid of U_{0,3} on rational base points should lift to vertex-fixing automorphisms of the groupoids of all K-defined covers, on their K-rational fibre points, up to powers. This is close in spirit to Pop's I/OM-type conditions and differs from Drinfeld's GT, which is built from the genus-0 Teichmüller tower. The substance is on the following page; this page only sets up the equivariant-groupoid framework.
missed.quote: l'étude des relations entre Π̂_1(C; I) et Π̂_1(U_{0,3}, I_0) [en] tant que groupoïdes à groupe d'opérateurs Γ, est facilité grandement en remplaçant I par son saturé I'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early version (~1978–81) of 'rational points as vertices give arithmetic constraints' for characterizing G_Q. It is of historical interest for the GT / I/OM line, though probably not new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine technical step: faithfulness of the groupoid functor for a finite étale cover, saturation of base points, and shrinking Γ. It feeds into a Belyi-type reduction already present in the Esquisse. The mildly interesting characterization condition is on the next page.
transcription_corrections: The groupoid is written Π̂_1(U_{0,3}) (U, not M) throughout.
'nous ne m'oubligerait' is likely 'rien ne m'obligerait à remplacer I par I''.
'J'aurais pu dire, car la saturation' is perhaps 'J'aurais pu éviter[?], car la saturée I' de I dans C n'est pas toute contenue dans C_K'.
'Mais il est vrai seulement que' is likely 'Mais il est vrai néanmoins que'.
'[?] tant que groupoïdes : groupe d'opérations [?] Γ' is likely 'en tant que groupoïdes à groupe d'opérateurs Γ'.
'si on est [?] par des moments que se brouillant sans l'action de Γ' is likely 'si on est gêné par des sommets qui se baladent sous l'action de Γ'.
On the previous page, 'Π_1(X,I) apparaît comme un sous-groupe de Π_1(C,I)' is likely 'quotient', if C is the punctured open part of X.
